limitations: Equation numbers restart at 1 in nearly every subsection, and the symbols are stripped.
Table 3 has an unlabeled row, Table 4 has blank hour bins, and Table 6 has blank parameter names.
Figure callouts run one number behind the figures they discuss.
The flyer percent 23.17 is not derived in the body.
Page 25 is a designed flyer with no text layer.

tasks: Build a light-pollution index and a risk level from economy, ecology, and health
Apply the risk to Saskatoon and classify the grids
Compare a grid move, a lighting regulation, and a tax
Write a flyer that promotes the regulatory strategy

section_map.summary: A question about the last starry sky, four community scores, and a regulatory winner.
A line of Frost, then the claim that light pollution still sits in the dark.
Unnamed factors are small, international data are trusted, and a border grid takes the larger type.
A Volterra damage, an entropy weighting, and a kernel that sums to one.
A Douglas night economy, a bent Gleason curve, a linear health line, and crime dropped.
A heat map, five risk bands, and a thin tail called the Pareto principle.
A grid swap, a 1 percent and 3 percent cut, and a tax that can rebound.
The lost sky, a 23.17 percent claim, and a beam aimed down.

contributions.summary: The weighted index is called narrow, and a kernel that sums to one is what widens it.
Crime is argued from a national comparison and then dropped.
Luminance is cut more slowly than the other lighting terms, and both rates are printed.
The tax is shown to rebound, and the advice splits: regulate hard, tax moderately.

dependency_graph.handoff: The wide light index is what the night economy, the diversity curve, and the health line take as input.
The grid risk is what the annealing search sums and tries to lower.
The grid risk is what regulation and the tax are judged by, at the same intensity.

assumptions.summary: Factors not named have a small impact, so they are left out.
Online databases are accurate because they are called international organizations.
A grid on a boundary takes the type that occupies most of it, and the error is ignored.
A very strong light held for a very short time does not pollute.
Technology does not change with time, and the pollution cost is linear in the index.
A moved grid carries its indicators, and must sit among eight grids of its own type.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Satellite lights, a dark-sky group, a pollution map, and scholar search are tabled, and the columns are shifted.
Color and flicker corrections are tabulated by grid type, from 0.1645 and 0.1623 down to zero.
Three years from 15 regions are standardized, and time is scored 1, 0.67, and 0.33.
Saskatoon and its suburb, plus one rural community and one protected land, are gridded from the city plan.

models.summary: A raster light index: Volterra damage, entropy weights 85.73, 4.82, and 9.45, then a neighbor kernel.
A Douglas night economy, a bent Gleason diversity, a linear health line, and an unprinted hierarchy.
An annealing swap that minimizes the risk sum, under an eight-neighbor rule.
A five-level intensity that cuts luminance 1 percent and the other terms 3 percent, set against a tax.

verification.summary: The night economy is fit by maximum likelihood, returning 0.4356, 345.4, and -5.007.
A judgment matrix and a consistency ratio are mentioned, and the weights are not shown.
The swapped layout is checked against the familiar center-to-edge order.
The commercial spill is swept from 0.04 to 0.06 by 0.002, and the risk barely moves.

results_trace.summary: Damage takes 85.73 percent of the narrow index.
Extreme risk sits in the commercial grids, and the suburb has no extreme and no high band.
Commercial grids cluster downtown, and the move is refused for a built city.
Regulation wins at every intensity, and the tax rebounds in two district types.
The flyer claims a 23.17 percent cut at the source.

writing_logic.summary: Ask when the reader last saw a starry sky, then give the four communities in one breath.
Drop a factor and give the reason in the same bullet.
Call the index narrow, say why, and only then widen it.
Argue an indicator, then drop it.
Warn that an average is not a rigorous risk.
Make one cut harder than the others, and give both rates.
Say the stronger the rule the better, and the tax should be moderate.
On the flyer, put the lost sky before the percent.

language_observations.summary: A poem line comes before the problem, and the issue is said to sit in the dark.
A short strong light is refused by an appeal to classical physical theory.
The index is called narrow because the commercial grid spills.
The subjective weight is preferred because the objective one cannot see the criteria.
A thin tail is called the Pareto principle.
The move is not recommended, and then it is kept for a new city.
The public piece closes on aiming the beam down.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A judge rewards calling an index narrow and then widening it, because the spill is the reason.
A judge rewards a team that argues crime and then drops it, with the national comparison named.
A judge rewards splitting the advice, hard regulation and a moderate tax, after the rebound is located.
A judge penalizes a risk built on hierarchy weights that never print.
A judge penalizes a 23.17 percent claim that the body does not derive, and a flyer that restores crime after the model dropped it.

weaknesses.summary: Eight grids in the summary do not match the four-type raster, and the risk name flips between LPRI and LPRL.
The Volterra equation prints blank, and Table 3 has an unlabeled row.
The hour bins behind 1, 0.67, and 0.33 do not print.
The three fitted values have no parameter names.
The hierarchy weights do not print.
Figure callouts run one number behind the figures.
The annealing acceptance test prints empty.
The compensation intensity words do not match the regulatory ones.
Sensitivity moves only the commercial spill.
The flyer quotes 23.17 percent with no derivation, and puts crime back among the harms.

independent_extensions.statement: Print the hierarchy weights and recompute whether regulation still beats the tax once the weights are visible.
independent_extensions.reason: The ranking of the two policies depends on a weighted risk whose weights do not print.

independent_extensions.statement: Derive the flyer claim of a 23.17 percent cut from the intensity sweep, or remove it.
independent_extensions.reason: The percent is not in the body, so the public piece is stronger than the model.

candidate_rule_impacts.impact: Supports a damage score that rises with luminance and levels off, and an intensity sweep that recomputes the risk.
Supports a night-economy function net of a linear light cost, and a tax that can raise the risk again if it is pushed too far.

unresolved_questions: Which of 0.4356, 345.4, and -5.007 is the brightness share.
What the hierarchy weights of economy, diversity, and health are.
Where the flyer figure of 23.17 percent is computed.
